This Privacy Policy explains the information BulkBro processes, why it is used, and the services involved when you use the app.
Depending on the features you use, BulkBro may process information such as:
This information is used to provide BulkBro’s tracking, calorie-target, progress, and weekly adaptive-target functionality.
Much of BulkBro’s personal tracking state is stored locally on the user’s device.
This includes tracking and progress information required for the app to operate.
Deleting the app may remove locally stored information unless that information is otherwise retained through Apple, a connected service, or device backup.
BulkBro may also provide in-app controls for deleting locally stored app data.

With your permission, the meal description you submit—including reviewed text from voice input—is sent to BulkBro’s Google Firebase backend and OpenAI to estimate nutrition. Your weight history and profile are not included in these requests.

If you choose photo meal estimation and grant its separate consent, a photo you select or capture is resized and converted to JPEG on your device, then sent to BulkBro’s Firebase backend and OpenAI to estimate nutrition. The submitted photo is not saved in your food log or reusable estimate cache, although the resulting estimate and technical request records may be retained as described below.

You can decline and use manual calories or saved meals. You can withdraw permission in Settings under AI meal estimates. Withdrawing permission stops future requests; it does not delete previously processed data.

Firebase stores estimated meal responses and technical request records under identifiers derived from your anonymous app account for request deduplication, abuse prevention, and caching. These records are associated with that account even though you do not enter an email address. Cache reuse is limited to 30 days; this is not a guarantee that stored records are deleted after 30 days. Contact
for a data-deletion request. Google and OpenAI also process information under their respective privacy and retention policies.
AI estimates may include calories, protein, portions, and related meal information. Review estimates before saving. BulkBro does not use AI meal estimation to provide a medical diagnosis.
If a user chooses to describe a meal using speech, BulkBro uses Apple’s speech-recognition functionality to convert speech into text.
Microphone and speech-recognition permissions are controlled by iOS.
The resulting meal-description text may then be processed in the same way as typed meal text for AI-assisted meal estimation.
BulkBro’s adaptive calorie engine calculates the next calorie target from the current completed seven-day week.
For an evaluated week, the calculation uses:
average calorie intake across the seven explicitly completed daily logs;
opening and closing weight for that week;
Previous weekly results and historical weights are not used to calculate the next calorie target.
Historical weights, calorie targets, and weekly results may remain stored on your device for progress history, Learning information, and other app features.

The adaptive calorie engine is application logic and is not an AI medical diagnosis system. Your complete weight history is not sent to an AI provider for this calorie-target calculation, and the adaptive calorie target is not AI-generated.
BulkBro uses analytics and app-measurement services to understand product usage, measure events, diagnose product issues, and improve the app.
Apple-provided App Store and subscription services;
Apple Ads attribution for measuring Apple Search Ads campaigns;
Meta App Events for limited advertising measurement, only when you grant Apple’s tracking permission.
Depending on the service and device settings, information may include app interactions, device/app information, purchase or subscription events, and similar usage information.

If you grant permission through Apple’s App Tracking Transparency prompt, BulkBro may use the advertising identifier (IDFA) with Meta App Events to measure whether an advertising campaign led to an app open, completed onboarding, paywall view, or subscription. If you decline, Meta advertising measurement remains disabled. Your choice does not affect app features.
BulkBro never sends meal descriptions, calorie intake, weight entries, targets, progress, health information, or profile answers to Meta.
Apple Ads attribution may provide campaign-level identifiers for an install attributed to an Apple Search Ads campaign. BulkBro uses this information for aggregate acquisition measurement.
BulkBro uses Firebase-related infrastructure for functions including:
Firebase Authentication and App Check may process technical identifiers or tokens necessary to authenticate or protect requests.
Firebase Authentication does not necessarily mean a user creates a normal visible BulkBro account.
Paid BulkBro subscriptions are processed through Apple’s App Store and StoreKit. BulkBro uses RevenueCat to help manage subscription and entitlement status.
BulkBro and RevenueCat may process information such as an anonymous app user identifier, product selection, subscription status, entitlement state, and purchase events.
This information is used to provide paid functionality and measure subscription performance.
BulkBro and RevenueCat do not receive or store your full payment-card details for App Store purchases. Apple processes payment information according to Apple’s own terms and privacy practices.
If notifications are enabled, BulkBro may schedule local reminders on the user’s device.
Notification permission is controlled through iOS settings.
BulkBro processes information as necessary to:
maintain seven-day tracking weeks and weekly calorie-target updates;
BulkBro relies on third-party platforms and services that may process information under their own privacy terms.
These may include Apple, Google/Firebase, Meta, OpenAI, RevenueCat, and infrastructure involved in AI-assisted meal estimation.
The information processed by each service depends on the feature used and the user’s device/privacy settings.
Locally stored BulkBro data remains on the device until deleted through the app, removed with the app where applicable, or otherwise removed through device-management mechanisms.
Third-party providers may retain information according to their own policies and retention requirements.
Where BulkBro provides a Delete Everything control, it is intended to remove BulkBro’s locally stored user data and reset applicable local app state.
It cannot necessarily delete information independently retained by Apple or other third-party services.
BulkBro uses reasonable technical measures and platform security features intended to protect information.
No method of electronic storage or transmission can be guaranteed to be completely secure.
BulkBro is not intended for children under 13.
Users under 18 should not use BulkBro for weight-gain planning without appropriate involvement from a parent or guardian and, where appropriate, a qualified healthcare professional.
BulkBro may update this Privacy Policy as the product, technology, or legal requirements change.
The updated policy will display a revised Last Updated date.

children: How Bump Echo handles your Soundbook, recordings, pregnancy details and limited technical information.
Bump Echo is provided by Kenneth Marcel S De Geest, a self-employed developer based in Spain. Privacy and support questions may be sent to

The app stores the profile details you enter, including a parent name, optional baby name, estimated due date, onboarding preferences and language preference. It also stores your audio recordings, recording dates and durations, titles, notes, favourites, search state and other settings needed to operate your Soundbook.
This content is stored in the app’s local storage on your iPhone. Bump Echo does not upload recordings, titles, notes, names or pregnancy details to a developer-operated server.
Bump Echo requests microphone permission only when you choose to record. Audio is captured to create the memory you requested. You can change microphone access at any time in iOS Settings.
The microphone-level display represents ordinary audio input strength. Bump Echo does not identify a fetal heartbeat, measure heart rate, diagnose a condition or assess pregnancy or fetal wellbeing.

Nothing is shared automatically. When you use the iOS share sheet, the selected audio file is passed to the app, service or recipient you choose; their privacy practices then apply. Copies already shared are outside Bump Echo’s control.
Apple device or iCloud backups may include app data depending on your Apple settings. Apple processes backup information under its own privacy terms.
Analytics, diagnostics, purchases and cancellation feedback

Bump Echo uses Firebase Analytics for anonymous app, paywall, plan-selection, purchase and cancellation events; Firebase Crashlytics for reliability diagnostics; RevenueCat for purchase and entitlement status; and Apple for StoreKit transactions, billing, refunds and purchase restoration.

If you explicitly cancel Apple’s purchase sheet, Bump Echo may show an optional, non-blocking survey once on that installation. If you answer, Firebase receives only a stable general reason: too expensive, prefer a subscription, need to try it first, not sure what is included, or something else. Choosing “Not now” sends no survey reason. The survey never collects free text.

Depending on the service and your settings, these providers may process pseudonymous identifiers, app interaction events, product or plan identifiers, device and operating-system information, country or region, crash logs, diagnostics, purchase events and access status. They do not receive your recordings, titles, notes, names, pregnancy information, family details or email address from these app events.
Bump Echo does not receive full payment-card details, sell personal information or use app data to track you across apps or websites owned by other companies.

Information is processed only as needed to provide and personalise the Soundbook, record and replay audio, save and organise memories, share content at your request, verify access, restore purchases, maintain security, diagnose crashes, understand feature usage, provide support and improve Bump Echo.

Local recordings and related details remain on your device until you delete an individual memory or remove the app. An unfinished but playable recording may be recovered after an unexpected app exit so it is not silently lost.

Removing the app normally removes its local container, but device backups and previously shared copies must be managed separately. Firebase, RevenueCat and Apple retain limited service information according to their own rules and legal obligations. Because Bump Echo has no user account or developer-hosted recording library, the developer cannot remotely access or delete content that exists only on your device.

Bump Echo uses iOS storage and platform security features intended to protect local information. No storage or transmission method can be guaranteed completely secure. Service providers may process technical and purchase information outside your country, subject to their safeguards and applicable law.
Bump Echo is intended for expecting parents and families, not children under 13. A minor should use the app only with permission and appropriate supervision from a parent or legal guardian.

You can deny or revoke microphone permission, edit profile information, delete memories, remove the app, choose whether to share a recording, and manage subscriptions through your Apple Account settings. Lifetime purchases do not renew. Buying lifetime access does not cancel an existing subscription.
For a privacy request or question, contact
. Requests concerning Apple, Firebase or RevenueCat data may also need to be directed to that provider.
This policy may be updated when Bump Echo’s features, service providers or legal requirements change. The effective date above identifies the current version.

children: Which information leaves your iPhone, why it is needed, who can see it and how you can control or delete it.
WalkBop is provided by Kenneth Marcel S De Geest, a self-employed developer (autónomo) based in Spain. For privacy questions or requests, email

WalkBop uses Sign in with Apple. The service receives an Apple-linked account identifier and may receive your name and email address, including an Apple private-relay address if you choose Hide My Email. WalkBop stores your display name, unique handle, internal account identifier and character appearance.

If you grant Apple Health access, WalkBop reads step-count samples needed to calculate your current weekly total. It sends the weekly total—not the individual Health samples—to its service so races, positions, results and rewards work across participating accounts.
WalkBop stores invitations, friendships, race participation and results, rank movement, item inventory, item use and effects, mystery-crate progress and related game events.
If you enable alerts, WalkBop stores a Firebase installation identifier, alert preferences and delivery records needed for race, friend, item, crate and result notifications.

Privacy-conscious analytics, crash reports and performance measurements can include app interactions, app version, device and operating-system details, performance timing and crash diagnostics. Individual Health samples and support-message contents are not sent to analytics.
If you email support, the address, message, attachments and related delivery information are processed to respond to and manage the request.

WalkBop keeps limited preferences and temporary state on the device, such as onboarding completion, the locally displayed character, handled race-result markers, staged invitation or notification routes and local notification state. Apple Health retains the underlying Health records. WalkBop does not upload individual step samples or write Health data.

Deleting your WalkBop account clears WalkBop-controlled local account data. Removing the app also removes its ordinary local data, subject to Apple device-backup behaviour. Apple Health records remain under your control in Apple Health.

Why don’t my steps match Apple Health?

WalkBop reads steps from Apple Health and refreshes your weekly total. Recent steps can take a moment to appear. Check that WalkBop can read Steps in Apple Health or iPhone Settings, then reopen the app. WalkBop cannot reconstruct steps missing from Apple Health.
Your Apple Health steps become race points. Races reset each week, and your position changes as friends walk and use items. A friend may briefly show an older score until their app syncs again.

These targets are estimates intended for general fitness guidance. Human metabolism varies, and the quality of BulkBro’s guidance depends on the accuracy and consistency of the information you enter.

Weight measurements can fluctuate because of hydration, food intake, glycogen, sodium, measurement timing, and other factors. Calorie tracking can also contain estimation or logging errors. BulkBro cannot guarantee that a calorie target will produce a particular amount or rate of weight gain.

If you experience concerning symptoms or unexpected changes in your health or weight, stop relying on the app for guidance and contact an appropriate healthcare professional. For an urgent or life-threatening concern, contact local emergency services.
